title: Charlie Holmes, Sam Taylor and Bob Dorsey
summary: Cootie's saxophones included Charlie Holmes, Bob Dorsey and Sam The Man Taylor, who got few solos.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Yeah. That's terrific. Well, when you had Charlie Holmes, cause it's in a sense like having Johnny in a way.
Because he does sound very like Johnny, doesn't he?
He must model himself on Johnny, I guess, huh?
Yeah. Both of them came from Boston.
Oh, they did. I didn't realize that. Yeah. Well, so when you -- oh, well -- Cleanhead wasn't in the band at that time? No, that's right. As you say, he went in the Army, didn't he?
And Bob Dorsey and Sam Taylor. Oh, yeah. Those were your four saxophones. Well, what -- what about Sam "The Man" Taylor? Is he still around?
No kidding. Was he hard to handle?
No. He wasn't hard to handle. A perfect gentleman.
And what did -- did Bob Dorsey play -- was he baritone, or something?
Sam the Man didn't get a chance to play then.
I don't know. I didn't like his sound then.
In that era. No. Bob Dorsey used to have all the solos.
Do you laugh at yourself now?
Isn't that funny. Well, what kind of a sound did Sam Taylor get, then? You mean it was a different tone?
Yeah. A different sound or something. But Bob Dorsey used to play all the solos.
That's funny. That must have irked Sam Taylor, mustn't it?
He must have been dying to blow, huh?
Did he stay with you long?
